name: Estate sale company and auctioneer

story.A: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex brings 14 pieces to Lee Gallery, Sam's consignment and appraisal gallery, and Odette logs them for the next auction on Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am. The visit depends on the money choice you pick. Pick one at the top to follow its path from start to end.
story.B: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books Lee Estate Sales for a free walk-through of the house Alex is clearing at 55 Orchard Ln. Gil comes Thu Oct 22 at 9am, sends a written proposal, and runs setup, three sale days and the settlement once the agreement is signed. The money choice you pick changes the path.

examples.list|none|none: A consignment drop-off or a free 15-minute evaluation. Nothing is taken. The gallery keeps 25% of what sells and settles the rest after the auction, its own way.
examples.list|card|counter: A written appraisal at the office, 2-hour minimum $350; a card saved for the $50 missed-appointment fee; paid at the counter.

examples.visit|none|own: The main story: a free walk-through, then a managed estate sale: 35% of the gross, $1,500 minimum, taken from the proceeds; nothing up front. Lee Estate Sales settles it its own way within 14 days of the last sale day. Rosie sends nothing about money.
examples.visit|none|bill: A cleanout quoted at the walk-through when there's no sale: $900, nothing up front, billed through Rosie after the job.
examples.list|none|bill: A written appraisal at the home, $175 an hour with a 2-hour minimum ($350); billed after.

notes:
New profession (P3 pass, Tue Oct 27 2026, batch P6), started from the refitted junk (from: junk), merged with the verified Oct 24 test-drive plug-in (work/testdrive/estate-sale.md, 11 findings, all general). Junk's haul-away steps (won't-take list, truck space, dump runs, curbside) were not carried; the structure is a project (a walk-through, a written proposal, a signed agreement, setup days, sale days, a settlement) built on the same master steps the contractor-style professions use.
Money: nothing up front. The firm is paid a share of what sells (a managed sale 35% of the gross with a $1,500 minimum, an on-site auction 30%, example), taken from the proceeds and settled in its own tools within 14 days of the last sale day; so no money goes through Rosie on the main path (visit|none|own) and Rosie texts only that the settlement statement is ready (amount on the secure page). Two paths do go through Rosie: a cleanout quoted at the walk-through ($900 example, nothing up front, billed after DONE) and a written appraisal at the home ($175 an hour, 2-hour minimum = $350, billed after). A cancel after setup has started owes the setup hours done at $45 a worker-hour (example), billed the business's own way; before setup nothing is owed.
Flow B main path visit|none|own: Alex (the person with the right to sell) clearing the house at 55 Orchard Ln. Free walk-through Thu Oct 22, 9am (Gil, set start); proof of the right to sell shown there (Rosie keeps only that it was shown); proposal Fri Oct 23 after Sam's OK; agreement Mon Oct 26 (Alex, and every co-executor or co-owner the business asks for) and Tue Oct 27 (Sam); cancel window to 11:59pm Mon Nov 2 (switch cancelright, flow B only). Own step B8-x01 Wed Nov 4: the family's kept items out by Wed Nov 11, the per-sale local permit (business) and the building's OK (family) before the sale is advertised. Work plan B8-37 (Wed Nov 4): setup Thu Nov 12 to Wed Nov 18, sale Fri Nov 20 to Sun Nov 22, cleanup Mon Nov 23, settlement by Sun Dec 6. B8-x02 (a branch of B8-22) Mon Nov 16: the family calls off the sale after setup began. B9-x01 Sun Dec 6: the settlement statement is ready. Rating once, only after the settlement (B10-02, Mon Dec 7).
Flow A is Sam's second company Lee Gallery (consignment, free evaluations, written appraisals; appraisers Odette and Felix). Paths: list|none|none (main: a consignment drop-off or a free evaluation: nothing taken; the gallery keeps 25% of what sells, settled after the auction) and list|card|counter (a written appraisal at the office, 2-hour minimum $350, card saved for a $50 missed-appointment fee, paid at the counter). A8-x01 logs the items (they stay for the next auction, they are not picked up); A8-x02 offers the free walk-through, which runs in flow B. Cards name 'an appraisal visit' on every A path (the master hard-codes one service name per flow).
Safety: stop = someone hurt, fallen or can't breathe; fire, smoke, gas smell. Steps then go on = an unreported death at home, a biohazard, mold, hoarding or unsafe stairs (a cleanup company first, none named; no entry until cleared), firearms and medicines (never sold; the family removes them), a pet left in the home, a grieving family (no sales talk). B3-11 and B3-18 are one Spanish conversation about mold in a basement. Rosie and staff give no advice on what an item is worth.
Who may book and sign: an adult; the agreement is signed only by people with the right to sell (owner, executor or administrator, trustee, financial power-of-attorney agent, conservator) and every co-owner or co-executor the business asks for; a power of attorney ends at death (then only the executor). Never a minor. A named specialist is not replaced on silence. Never in texts: lockbox and gate codes, item lists and values, the settlement amount, that a home stands empty (told only to the staff on the job), a death or why a home is being sold.
Licenses: an auctioneer license for each auctioneer (and/or the firm) where the state's rules license auctioneers; a bond and trust account for buyers' money where required; a used-goods dealer license or seller's permit and a per-sale local permit only where required; an auction stand-in must hold the same license. S1-60 and S2-28 are kept both ways. Example license numbers use the EX-2210 format.
Switches: cancelright (B). Facts: firststeps, documents, multiday, extrawork, results (the settlement statement is a report promised by a date). Settings: set start times in both flows; cutoff 24 hours. Not set: sensitive, welfare, standin, fixeddate.
The old test-drive gaps: nine are closed by the REDESIGN 2 master (partway stop B8-80, named person S13-56, call summary B3-22, rating split B10-32, nobody-home DONE B8-41, customer-side first step cut, need-by date B4-94, everyone signs B8-62, a death B7-73); two stay open (work/gaps/estate-sale.json). keep: leak, estate, house call, Hugo, cleanout, crew lead, hand truck.

pf.visit.check_in: The check-in code from whoever meets the specialist at the door; with nobody home on setup and sale days, a start photo and DONE with photos. At the gallery: the code at the desk.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The specialist walks the home, sees what can sell, and sends a written proposal on the secure page within 3 business days
pf.visit.changes: A new service added later (a cleanout, a buyout, an appraisal of one piece) is priced first and signed first
pf.visit.found_items: Cash, jewelry, papers and keepsakes found while setting up are shown to the person with the right to sell on the secure page, logged with a photo, and never sold, thrown away or taken by staff
pf.visit.done: Setup ends when the sale is ready. Each sale day ends with DONE. The sale ends with the settlement statement.
pf.visit.gallery_done: DONE after the drop-off or the appraisal, with the items logged on the secure page
pf.visit.items: Item lists, values and the settlement amount are on the secure page only; that a home stands empty is told only to the staff on the job

pf.money.walkthrough: free; nothing taken and nothing owed
pf.money.commission: The commission comes out of the proceeds. It is paid and settled in the firm's own tools, not through Rosie.
pf.money.settlement: The settlement statement and payment are due within 14 days of the last sale day (example). Rosie texts only that it is ready; the amount is on the secure page.
pf.money.cleanout: A cleanout quoted at the walk-through is billed through Rosie after the job; nothing is taken up front.
pf.money.cancel: A cancel after setup has started owes the setup hours done, at $45 a worker-hour (example), billed the business's own way. A cancel before setup owes nothing.
pf.money.gallery: A consignment owes nothing at drop-off. A written appraisal at the office saves a card for a $50 missed-appointment fee, kept only with the owner's yes.
pf.money.fee2: Rosfield's $2 applies: one per confirmed booking; a whole sale from one agreement is one job, so one $2
pf.money.no_advice: Rosie and its staff give no advice on what an item is worth or what to do with an estate

never_in_texts: Item lists, item values and the settlement amount: the secure page only
That a home stands empty: told only to the staff on the job
A death, health details or the family's situation: owner and staff texts never say why a home is being sold
pf.messages.rating: One rating, asked once, only after the settlement; none if the family asked for no follow-up

pf.staff.roles: Sale specialists (Gil, Irene) run each sale with a crew of 3; appraisers and auctioneers where the rules license them. At the gallery: appraisers Odette and Felix.
pf.staff.licenses: Each auctioneer holds the license the rules require; no other person license
pf.staff.who_oks: The owner OKs every proposal and any change to the commission
pf.staff.stand_in: The specialist the family asked for is not replaced on silence: a new person is offered only with the family's OK first. An auction stand-in must hold the same license.
pf.staff.never: Staff never buy from a sale they run, never accept gifts, and never sell firearms, medicines or found cash, jewelry or papers

pf.rules.agreement: A written agreement before setup, signed by every person with the right to sell, with the commission, the dates and the cancel terms; a written cancel period where the state's rules give one
pf.rules.authority: A power of attorney ends when the person dies; from then on, only the executor may sign
pf.rules.auction: An auction is run only by a licensed auctioneer where the rules require one
pf.rules.permit: A per-sale local permit where the rules require one
pf.rules.records: 7 years; sale records as long as the rules require

pf.edges.family_stops: The family stops the sale after setup has started: the setup hours done are owed (billed the business's own way) and the sale does not run; before setup nothing is owed
pf.edges.right_to_sell: Proof of the right to sell missing at the walk-through: the walk-through goes on, but the agreement can't be signed until it is shown
pf.edges.empty_by_date: A home that must be empty by a closing date: the sale days and the cleanout must end before it; if they can't, the family is told before signing
pf.edges.kept_items: Kept items not out by the day before setup, or the building's OK not in by the day before advertising: the family's side is late, so the date moves with no fee to the business's side
pf.edges.weather: A sale is not moved for rain; the owner can move a day
pf.edges.found_cash: Cash, jewelry or papers found: a note on the secure page, never in a text
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way
